atnf.selection: Reviewed or ATNF DIST <= 3.0660139380 kpc (10000 ly), and <= 0.9198041814 kpc when only a dispersion-measure model distance exists; no CAND or INTERIM type; verbatim psrcat.db records and their glitch.db rows

previous.change: Selection widened on 2026-11-05 from 3000 to 10000 light-years, requiring a distance independent of the dispersion-measure model beyond 3000 light-years. All 272 earlier pulsars remain selected.

blackcat.result: The live catalogue page was unreachable on 2026-11-05, so the catalogue paper and newer primary literature were reviewed; GRS 1716-249 was excluded after its distance was revised to 6.9 kpc.

reviewedBinaries.policy: Only individually measured pulsar and neutron-star companion masses from relativistic timing or optical spectroscopy, keyed by exact ATNF PSRJ name. Total-mass-only systems and model-dependent X-ray mass fits are not split into component masses.

J0418+5732.note: ATNF lists no distance. The commonly assumed 2 kpc is not a measurement.

J0420-5022.note: ATNF lists no distance. An absorption estimate, not a parallax.

J1012+5307.note: Replaces ATNF's 0.70 kpc (Verbiest et al. 2012); MSPSRpi Table 6 gives 0.877(35) kpc.

notes: ATNF DIST is the catalogue-adopted distance: DIST_A, else a parallax above 3 sigma, else the YMW16 dispersion-measure distance bounded by DIST_AMN/DIST_AMX.
Derived spin quantities follow psrcat v1.54 with a 10^45 g cm^2 moment of inertia; companion minimum and median masses assume a 1.35 M_sun pulsar at 90 and 60 degrees inclination.
ATNF companion mass limits are not stored as pulsar masses; measured pulsar masses come only from the reviewed binary list.

A reviewed distance replaces the ATNF DIST only where ATNF rests on a measurement newer work supersedes, or on an error; a superseded ATNF value stays in the record's notes, and an erroneous one stays only in the review files.
Modelled masses are kept apart from mass_solar in compact.mass_model and are never used as measurements.
An ATNF uncertainty of 0 means no uncertainty was reported and is stored as null.
Millisecond marks spin periods below 30 ms; Radio marks pulsars without the ATNF NRAD or XINS radio-quiet codes; other classes come from ATNF TYPE codes.
Gaia NS1 remains explicitly marked as a candidate because a close double-white-dwarf alternative is disfavored but not fully excluded.
Black-hole X-ray transients were reviewed from the BlackCAT catalogue paper and newer primary literature; the live BlackCAT page was unreachable on 2026-11-05.
A published mass range or asymmetric interval is stored as its midpoint or the larger side, as each record's notes state.
